title: notiongit-sync run summary
description: Machine-readable summary of one notiongit-sync run. See ../docs/run-summary-schema.md for the field-by-field guide, the result/code table and example payloads.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema. 1 for every payload this document describes; bumped only for a breaking change to this shape.

result.description: Coarse, stable outcome of the run.

code.description: Specific, machine-readable reason for `result`. New codes may be added within schema_version 1 without a version bump; a consumer that sees an unrecognized code should fall back to handling it by `result` alone.

changed.description: true when any tracked file (_pages/, _posts/, _data/nav.yml, _data/home.yml, the managed lines of _config.yml, or a copied Notion file under assets/notion/) was created, updated, renamed or deleted this run. Independent of `result`: a row_errors or bulk_delete_guard failure reports changed:true when the rest of the run wrote files, and the calling workflow commits them. Always false for no_op and sync_error, where nothing is committed.

started_at.description: UTC timestamp, ISO 8601, when this run began (before any Notion API call).

finished_at.description: UTC timestamp, ISO 8601, when this run reached its terminal state.

detail.description: Safe, human-readable, single-line detail: counts only. Never contains a Notion token, database ID, raw API response, page title/body, or stack trace — any error text that could echo one is redacted to "[redacted]" before it reaches this field. Titles appear only in `affected` and `skipped`.

affected.description: Optional; present only when non-empty. The rows the site owner needs to look at: for row_errors the rows that were not published this run, for bulk_delete_guard the rows whose removal was held back. At most 20 entries. Titles of published (or formerly published) rows only; draft rows are never read.

skipped.description: Optional; present only when non-empty. Published rows that went live with something left out: a file over the size cap, a file type websites cannot show, a file Notion did not hand over, or blocks the site cannot show. At most 20 entries.

sectionCounts.description: Counts for one database section (pages or posts), or null when that section didn't run this time — either because the run aborted (missing_credentials and sync_error leave both pages and posts null) or, on an otherwise-complete run, because that database simply isn't configured (a posts-only or pages-only setup leaves the other one null). A documented fallback either way, not a missing value. `scheduled` and `skipped_blocks` are optional additions within schema_version 1.

scheduled.description: Optional. Published posts held back because their date is still ahead; they go live at the first run on or after that date.

skipped_blocks.description: Optional. Blocks left out of published rows because the site cannot show them.

dataFiles.description: Which of the three shared data/config files were rewritten this run, or null only when no section ran at all (a run that aborted before finishing any section). Whenever at least one section ran — even a posts-only run, which never touches these files — this is real data, not a fallback: it can legitimately be all-false.

title.description: The row's title as written in Notion, whitespace collapsed.

reason_code.description: Machine-readable reason. affected: duplicate_web_address, read_failed, unexpected, would_remove. skipped: file_too_large, file_type_unsupported, file_unavailable, blocks_unsupported. New codes may be added; show `reason` for an unknown one.

reason.description: A plain-language sentence for the code, in English. Dashboards should prefer their own wording keyed by reason_code.

count.description: skipped only: how many files or blocks of this kind were left out of the row.
